issues.description: Class SealSaloon: the problem statement / UML require a method named checkOrderReady(): void that orderMeal() should call to attempt serving queued orders. The solution implementation instead declares a method public void processOrders() and orderMeal() calls this.processOrders(). This is a naming inconsistency for the same conceptual operation (processing/serving queued orders) and can confuse students who map the UML and textual requirements to the implementation or to automated tests that expect the method name from the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artefacts. Either rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (and keep its behavior and visibility), or add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to processOrders() and update any references so the name in the UML/problem statement matches the implementation. Alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to use processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(), so all materials use the same identifier.
